tools.name: wait_for_new_message
tools.title: Wait For New Message
tools.description: Block until a new incoming private message from a non-bot user arrives, then return immediately with the list of chats that currently have pending (unprocessed) incoming messages. If nothing arrives within `timeout` seconds, returns {"event": false, "reason": "timeout"}. Lets the agent react to events instead of polling. Does NOT consume the pending set — use wait_for_settled_message to consume a debounced burst.

tools.name: wait_for_settled_message
tools.title: Wait For Settled Message
tools.description: Event-driven, DEBOUNCED wait. Blocks until some private user chat has received one or more incoming messages AND then gone quiet for `settle_ms` — so a client who types several messages (or sends file + text) in a row is delivered as ONE settled burst instead of waking the agent on every message. Returns that chat's burst summary and removes it from the pending set, so the next call returns the next settled chat. If no chat settles within `max_wait_ms`, returns {"event": false, "reason": "timeout"} (caller should simply call again).

installMarkdown:
Requirements: [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Telegram credentials.
[Authenticate](#authenticate) explains how to get them. Run the published
package with an exact version pin:

```sh
uvx uniquedivine-telegram-mcp@2.0.2
```

The PyPI project is `uniquedivine-telegram-mcp`. Do not install the unrelated
PyPI project `telegram-mcp`. CI in
[Unique-Divine/jiyuu](https://github.com/Unique-Divine/jiyuu) builds and
publishes this package to PyPI from this directory when its version changes
on `main`. The version pin selects the exact reviewed release that runs.

Generate a session string with console script `telegram-mcp-generate-session`
from the same pinned package:

```sh
TELEGRAM_API_ID=123456 TELEGRAM_API_HASH=your_api_hash \
  uvx --from uniquedivine-telegram-mcp@2.0.2 telegram-mcp-generate-session --qr
```

The examples below pass credentials as environment variables. Keep the real
values out of version control.

### Claude Code

```sh
claude mcp add telegram \
  --env TELEGRAM_API_ID=123456 \
  --env TELEGRAM_API_HASH=your_api_hash \
  --env TELEGRAM_SESSION_STRING=your_session_string \
  -- uvx uniquedivine-telegram-mcp@2.0.2
```

### Codex

Add this entry to file `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.telegram]
command = "uvx"
args = ["uniquedivine-telegram-mcp@2.0.2"]

[mcp_servers.telegram.env]
TELEGRAM_API_ID = "123456"
TELEGRAM_API_HASH = "your_api_hash"
TELEGRAM_SESSION_STRING = "your_session_string"
```

### Cursor

Add this entry to file `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, or to file `.cursor/mcp.json` in
a project:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "telegram": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["uniquedivine-telegram-mcp@2.0.2"],
      "env": {
        "TELEGRAM_API_ID": "123456",
        "TELEGRAM_API_HASH": "your_api_hash",
        "TELEGRAM_SESSION_STRING": "your_session_string"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Update

1. Find the newest version at
   https://pypi.org/project/uniquedivine-telegram-mcp/ or with
   `curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/uniquedivine-telegram-mcp/json | jq -r .info.version`.
2. Change the `@2.0.2` pin in the client configuration to that version.
3. Restart the MCP server in the client, or restart the client. In Claude
   Code, run `/mcp` and reconnect the server. Command `uvx` installs the new
   version on the next launch.
